MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  APRIL 12, 2016

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:07 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
City Council Member Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Direct Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

Others Present:  Bob Schachter, Planning Commission

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION

  A PROCLAMATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES PROCLAIMING THE MONTH OF APRIL AS “DMV/DONATE LIFE
  CALIFORNIA MONTH”

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN presented a representative, who is the Donate Life
  Ambassador, with a Proclamation. She thanked the COUNCIL for their support
  and relayed her story about others benefitting from her late son’s donation.
  She further noted that there are three ways to register: 1) Department of Motor
  Vehicles; 2) Website at donatelifecalifornia.org; and 3) Participation at the
  Donate Life Run/Walk scheduled for April 30.

B.  PROCLAMATION

  A PROCLAMATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES PROCLAIMING APRIL 24, 2016 AS A “DAY OF REMEMBRANCE” OF
  THE ARMENIAN GENOCIDE OF 1915-1923

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN presented Raffy Mardirossian, Chair, Lomita Chapter of
  the South Bay Armenian Community Center, with a Proclamation.  Mr.
  Mardirossian noted his appreciation to the City for acknowledging this tragic
  event.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN commented on his appreciation to the COUNCIL
  for their support. He provided an extensive history of how this tragedy has
  affected him personally and emphasized his strong desire to eradicate these
  crimes against humanity for all ethnicities.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
APRIL 12, 2016
 5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL POLICY DEVELOPMENT MINUTES OF MARCH 5,
  2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO  APPROVE  THE  ADJOURNED  CITY  COUNCIL  POLICY
  DEVELOPMENT MINUTES OF MARCH 5, 2016 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 22, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 22, 2016 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – MARCH AND APRIL

  MAYOR PRO  TEM  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCILWOMAN
  MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 56637 THROUGH 56683 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $417,608.06; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 030116
  THROUGH 030216; 43841 (VOID); 52053 (VOID); 56489
  THROUGH 56549; 56540 (VOID); 56588 THROUGH 56623 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $384,987.51 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $802,595.57 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  NONE

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  Monique Sugimoto, Archivist and Adult Services Librarian, Palos Verdes Library
  District, announced their “Your Story is the Peninsula’s Story” project
  undertaken by the Local History Center.  She noted that residents are
  encouraged to share photographs representing their lives on the Peninsula
  which will scanned into their digital archives. She then announced a “Photo
  Scanning Event” will be held on April 30 at the Malaga Cove Library. Finally,
  she thanked staff for submitting photos which will be a valuable resource for
  generations to come.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN suggested Ms. Sugimoto contact the School
  District as an additional resource.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 12, 2016
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-07-16; APPLICANT: THE CHADMAR GROUP
  AND ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB; LOCATION 26311 AND 27000 PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST; REQUEST TO AMEND CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION
  NO. 2260 (CONDITION OF APPROVAL NO. 68); APPROVAL OF A NEW BRIDLE
  TRAIL AND LANDSCAPE EASEMENT; SEWER EASEMENT; AND TEMPORARY
  PARKING LOT LOCATED AT THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

  Recommendation:  That the City Council:  1)  Continue to take public
  testimony; 2) Discuss the issues; 3) Close the public hearing; and 4) Approve
  the Easement Agreement for June’s Trail to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that Planning Director Wahba has worked
  with the Applicant to provide added space on the trail.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, Planning Director Wahba noted
  that the Traffic Engineer is confident larger vehicles will be able to pass through
  on the trail.

  Discussion ensued regarding the hydrology issue on June’s Trail and other
  locations where storm drains are problematic. Planning Director Wahba noted
  that on April 26 a proposal from Willdan Engineering will be presented to the
  COUNCIL and will make sure that affected neighborhoods are involved in the
  process.

  Paul Schwartz, 13 Sorrel Lane, commented that he would like to maintain the
  trail as currently exists and asked the COUNCIL to keep this in mind with
  respect to the golf course. He provided a brief history of DLPOA efforts. He
  then requested that the COUNCIL address the drainage issues first and then
  make a decision on the easement at a later date.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL commented that the developer has been more
  than generous in providing this easement and was confident that a drainage
  solution would be reached. She further stated that, while she understands
  more space is desired, she has had personal experience in horse keeping
  without vehicle access and was certain that the affected properties would be
  adequately served by the trail easement under consideration.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN concurred with COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL
  and also thanked the neighbors who were involved in this process to make sure
  that the concerns of the DLPOA are addressed. He further noted that Mr.
  Lande understands the importance of the equestrian lifestyle to the City and
  that he is confident he will work with staff to solve any further issues. Finally,
  he stated that he is certain that the completed golf course and development will
  be valuable assets to the City and he thanked the staff for their efforts.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that everyone involved has worked together to
  create a positive outcome.

  COUNCILWOMAN  MITCHELL  moved,  seconded  by  MAYOR  PRO  TEM
  ZERUNYAN

  TO APPROVE THE EASEMENT AGREEMENT FOR JUNE’S TRAIL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 12, 2016
 9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING OF MARCH 21,
  2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETING OF MARCH 21, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF MARCH 21, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF MARCH 21, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  MARCH 21, 2016 – THE HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the agreement with Michael
  Hogue Productions to provide fundraising, promotional, and consulting services
  for the 2016 Hills are Alive Race.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE AGREEMENT WITH MICHAEL HOGUE PRODUCTIONS
  TO PROVIDE FUNDRAISING, PROMOTIONAL, AND CONSULTING
  SERVICES FOR THE 2016 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

D.  CABLECAST BROADCASTING AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES AND THE CITY OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES REGARDING
  CABLECASTING ON PVPTV

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager to sign the
  agreement with the City of Rancho Palos Verdes to provide cable broadcast
  services for the City of Rolling Hills Estates on Palos Verdes Peninsula Television,
  Channel 35 and Fios Channel 39.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  noted that Rancho Palos Verdes has not charged the City for this service as yet.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  noted that the meetings will also be posted on the City’s website and that the City
  is preparing to undertake audio visual upgrades.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF inquired if other organizations are being charged by
  Rancho Palos Verdes for broadcast service. Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  noted that it is likely.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that the City is looking for the capability to
  stream live.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, City Attorney Davis noted that the
  AV upgrade project requires a bidding process.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 12, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO SIGN THE AGREEMENT WITH
  THE CITY OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES TO PROVIDE CABLE
  BROADCAST SERVICES FOR THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES ON
  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA TELEVISION, CHANNEL 35 AND FIOS
  CHANNEL 39.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

E.  SLURRY SEAL BID DOCUMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the solicitation of bids for the
  FY 2015-16 Slurry Seal Project.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that a bid package will be brought before the COUNCIL for street overlays
  as a separate project.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Assistant City Manager Grammer noted
  that the entry to Montecillo will not be part of this project, but will be scheduled
  for the Summer of 2017.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired if residents should be advised not to water their
  lawns on the same day as the project takes place and suggested signs be posted
  at the entryways. Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that the contractor will
  send a notice to every resident on the street and will include this suggestion.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE FY 2015-16 SLURRY
  SEAL PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MARCH 28, 2016 – COUNCILWOMAN
  SCHMITZ

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  MARCH 28, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 12, 2016
 B.  REGIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE MEETING OF MARCH 23, 2016 –
  AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE RECOGNITION (ALPR) CAMERA REGIONAL
  SYSTEM – MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the purchase and installation of
  Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) in the amount of $80,247.54 one-
  time cost and $2,060 ongoing cost in accordance with a Memorandum of
  Understanding (MOU) between the four Peninsula cities for the regional ALPR
  project to be formally approved by the City Council before June 24, 2016.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated
  that discussion by the city managers regarding setting aside funds to replace the
  system in five years will be up to each city.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, City Manager Prichard noted that a five-
  year Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was discussed at the staff level, and if
  a city elected not to continue with the program, there would be no additional
  obligation at the end of that term. He further noted that each city would likely
  maintain a reserve within their own budgets for replacement when needed.

  Discussion ensued regarding the preferred location for additional cameras on the
  east side of the Peninsula in Rancho Palos Verdes. It was noted that the issue will
  go before the Committee for a thorough analysis.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, City Manager Prichard explained
  the benefits of the cameras to address the increase in residential burglaries. He
  noted that the COUNCIL and Regional Law Committee approved the addition of a
  Surveillance and Apprehension Team (SAT) investigator as well. He further noted
  that the fixed cameras under consideration would be in addition to previously
  purchased mobile units that have the Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR)
  technology. He also noted that data gathered from the cameras can be shared
  with other law enforcement agencies. Finally, he was pleased to note that the City
  of Palos Verdes Estates Police Department is also participating in this program.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that this collaboration is a wise use of law
  enforcement funds.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN commented that, while the Sheriff’s Department
  does a fine job, the changing times warrant taking this step to prevent further
  crime.

  City Manager Prichard encouraged residents to become involved with
  Neighborhood Watch and noted that Assistant to the City Manager Davis and
  COUNCIL MEMBERS have attended various meetings.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that Community Resource Team (CORE)
  Deputies also attend to provide residents with strategies to better secure their
  properties.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO APPROVE THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF AUTOMATED
  LICENSE PLATE RECOGNITION (ALPR) IN THE AMOUNT OF $80,247.54
  ONE-TIME COST AND $2,060 ONGOING COST IN ACCORDANCE WITH A
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU) BETWEEN THE FOUR
  PENINSULA CITIES FOR THE REGIONAL ALPR PROJECT TO BE
  FORMALLY APPROVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL BEFORE JUNE 24, 2016
  AND REFERRED THE PURCHASE OF TWO ADDITIONAL CAMERAS TO
  THE REGIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE FOR DISCUSSION
  AND A RECOMMENDATION TO THE COUNCIL AT A FUTURE MEETING.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz
